summary:
[  edit  ]
The TCP/IP  DAT  is used for sending and receiving information over a TCP/IP connection between two remotely located computers. It captures all the messages without any queuing or buffering, and allows you to send it any messages you want.
Send messages using the  tcpipDAT_Class . Handle received messages using the callback  DAT  attached to the TCP/IP  DAT . See  Network Protocols .
This  DAT  can be used to intercept all the raw information being sent from a  Pipe  Out  CHOP  for example. The  Pipe In CHOP  and  Pipe Out CHOP  also communicate through a TCP/IP connection, though they use a specific syntax.
See also  Peer Class ,  UDP In DAT ,  UDP Out DAT .
For  Tscript . see  Tscript   send  Command.
NOTE for Windows OS - If experiencing connection issues make sure Windows Firewall is disabled.

parameters.label: Connection Mode
parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specify if this operator is communicating as a  client  or a  server .

parameters.label: Network Address
parameters.name: address
parameters.description: If this node is communicating as a client, this should be the IP address of the server.

parameters.label: Port
parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The network port to listen on or connect to, depending on of the node is the server or client respectively.

parameters.label: Shared Connection
parameters.name: shared
parameters.description: Use the same connection as other networking DATs using the same network protocol.

parameters.label: Row/ Callback  Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the incoming data is parsed into the table.

parameters.label: One Per Byte
parameters.name: perbyte
parameters.description: One row is added to the table per byte received.

parameters.label: One Per Line
parameters.name: perline
parameters.description: One row is added to the table per line received. The end of a line is delimited by \n, \r or a null character (\0).

parameters.label: One For All Received Data
parameters.name: all
parameters.description: One row is added to the table per message received. Since TCP/IP is a stream-based protocol, the end of a 'message' is arbitrary. It is simply the contents of the last read operation from the socket. If you are reading a custom message format, you'll likely need to build up a full message from multiple reads from the socket in Python.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: This check box enables the connection.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The Callbacks  DAT  will execute once for each message received.

parameters.label: Execute from
parameters.name: executeloc
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines the location the script is run from.

parameters.label: Current  Node
parameters.name: current
parameters.description: The script is executed from the current node location.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The script is executed from the location of the  DAT  specified in the   Script   DAT   parameter.

parameters.label: Specified  Operator
parameters.name: op
parameters.description: The script is executed from the component specified in the   Component   parameter below.

parameters.label: From  Operator
parameters.name: fromop
parameters.description: The component who's state change will trigger the  DAT  to execute its script when  Execute from  is set to  On Panel Change . This component is also the path that the script will be executed from if the  Execute from  parameter is set to  Specified  Component  .

parameters.label: Clamp Output
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: The  DAT  is limited to 100 messages by default but with Clamp Output, this can be set to anything including unlimited.

parameters.label: Maximum Lines
parameters.name: maxlines
parameters.description: Limits the number of messages, older messages are removed from the list first.

parameters.label: Clear Output
parameters.name: clear
parameters.description: Deletes all lines except the heading. To clear with a script command, here is an example:  opparm -c /serial1 clear

parameters.label: Bytes Column
parameters.name: bytes
parameters.description: Outputs the raw bytes of the message in a separate column.
